_source.abstract:
This ASCAT Multi-parameter product contains surface wind vectors over ocean and soil moisture index over land. Additionally, the backscatter values involved in the retrieval of the geophysical parameters above are also included, as well as several quality flags to facilitate the use of the data. For NWP users this product is provided in BUFR format. The netCDF version of this product contains Winds ONLY.

For users interested in either ASCAT backscatter, wind or soil moisture index data in other formats, please refer to the relevant product entries available for the specific parameters. Finally, note that although the OSI SAF is identified as the originating centre for this product, it is not responsible for the processing of soil moisture index values, which is currently carried out at EUMETSAT.

_source.abstract:
The SLSTR level 1 products contain:
- the radiances of the 6 visible (VIS), Near Infra-Red (NIR) and Short Wave Infra-Red (SWIR) bands (on the A and B stripe grids)
- the Brightness Temperature (BT) for the 3 Thermal Infra-Red (TIR) bands
- the BT for the 2 Fire (FIR) bands

Resolution: 1km at nadir (TIR), 500m (VIS). All are provided for both the oblique and nadir view. These measurements are accompanied with grid and time information, quality flags, error estimates and meteorological auxiliary data. Sentinel-3 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme. This collection contains reprocessed data from baseline collection 004. Operational data can be found in the corresponding collection.

_source.abstract:
The index covers time series of sea-ice extent and area, complemented by standard statistics, climate normals, anomalies and long-term trends. 
 The product consists of regularly updated data files (in netCDF and text formats) for users who wish to analyse and visualise the data themselves. In addition, graphical products (in PNG format) illustrate the evolution and long-term trends of sea ice at global, hemispheric and regional scales. 
 The Sea Ice Index is derived from the EUMETSAT OSI SAF Global Sea Ice Concentration data sets, developed with R&D contributions from ESA CCI.

_source.abstract:
Reprocessed level 1b data from the Advanced Scatterometer (ASCAT) on Metop-A, resampled at 12.5 km Swath Grid (SZR).

Normalized radar cross section (NRCS) triplets of the Earth surface together with:
- measurement time
- location (latitude and longitude)
- geometrical information (incidence and azimuth angles)

The prime objective of the Advanced SCATterometer (ASCAT) is to measure wind speed and direction over the oceans, and the main operational application is the assimilation of ocean winds in NWP models.

Other operational applications, based on the use of measurements of the backscattering coefficient, are:
- sea ice edge detection and monitoring
- monitoring sea ice
- snow cover
- soil moisture
- surface parameters

This product is also available at full resolution and at 25 km Swath Grid. This is a Fundamental Climate Data Record (FCDR).

_source.abstract:
Derived LST (DLST; LSA-003) provides a synthesis of the Meteosat Land Surface Temperature (MLST; LSA-001) products within a 10-day interval, consisting of two sub-products. LSA-003A contains the maximum and median MLST composites over this 10-day interval.

Like the well-known Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), MLST composites are simple subsets of the input quantity. Temporal composites usually have considerably fewer missing data and are spatially more continuous than the input data. The LSA-003A composites also serve as the direct input for the companion sub-product LSA-003B, which fits a diurnal temperature cycle model to these composites to derive a set of physically meaningful Thermal Surface Parameters (TSP).

_source.abstract:
The global total column water vapour (TCWV) data record combines microwave and near-infrared imager based TCWV over the ice-free ocean as well as over land, coastal ocean and sea-ice, respectively.

The data record relies on:
- microwave observations from SSM/I, SSMIS, AMSR-E and TMI, partly based on a fundamental climate data record (Fennig et al., 2020; Fennig et al., 2017)
- near-infrared observations from MERIS (3rd reprocessing), MODIS-Terra (collection 6.1) and OLCI (1st reprocessing)

Details of the retrieval are described in Andersson et al. (2010) and ATBD HOAPS for the microwave imagers as well as in Lindstrot et al. (2012), Diedrich et al. (2015) and ABTD NIR level 2 for the near-infrared imagers. The water vapour of the atmosphere is vertically integrated over the full column and given in units of kg/m².

The microwave and near-infrared data streams are processed independently and combined afterwards by not changing the individual TCWV values and their uncertainties. The combined data record has a spatial resolution of 0.5°x0.5° and 0.05°x0.05°, with the near-infrared based data being averaged and the microwave-based data being oversampled to match the lower and higher spatial resolution, respectively. The product is available as daily and monthly means and covers the period July 2002 – December 2017. This is a Thematic Climate Data Record (TCDR).

_source.abstract:
This is Release 1 of the Fundamental Data Record (FDR) brightness temperatures from the High Resolution Infrared Radiation Sounder (HIRS) on board NOAA and Metop satellites. The data record covers more than 40 years from 29 October 1978 to 31 December 2020. Release 1 provides recalibrated level 1c brightness temperatures based on the V4.0 calibration method developed by Cao et al. (2007). This method was implemented into the NWP-SAF software ATOVS and AVHRR processing Package (AAPP). This software was consistently used to recalibrate and reprocess data from all HIRS instruments on board TIROS-N, NOAA-06 to NOAA-19, Metop-A, and Metop-B.

The polygons, required for the data tailoring, show problems with non-continues data. Some polygons of the HIRS data record are found to be incorrect. However, this does not affect the correctness of the data itself. This is a Fundamental Data Record (FDR).

This is Release 1 of the Fundamental Data Record (FDR) brightness temperatures from the High Resolution Infrared Radiation Sounder (HIRS) on board NOAA and Metop satellites. The data record covers more than 40 years from 29 October 1978 to 31 December 2020. Release 1 provides recalibrated level 1c brightness temperatures based on the V4.0 calibration method developed by Cao et al. (2007). This method was implemented into the NWP-SAF software ATOVS and AVHRR processing Package (AAPP). This software was consistently used to recalibrate and reprocess data from all HIRS instruments on board TIROS-N, NOAA-06 to NOAA-19, Metop-A, and Metop-B.

The polygons, required for the data tailoring, show problems with non-continues data. Some polygons of the HIRS data record are found to be incorrect. However, this does not affect the correctness of the data itself. This is a Fundamental Data Record (FDR).

$schema ./collection_schema_v2-15.json hierarchyLevel series collectionType Dataset abstract This is Release 1 of the Fundamental Data Record (FDR) brightness temperatures from the High Resolution Infrared Radiation Sounder (HIRS) on board NOAA and Metop satellites. The data record covers more than 40 years from 29 October 1978 to 31 December 2020. Release 1 provides recalibrated level 1c brightness temperatures based on the V4.0 calibration method developed by Cao et al. (2007). This method was implemented into the NWP-SAF software ATOVS and AVHRR processing Package (AAPP). This software was consistently used to recalibrate and reprocess data from all HIRS instruments on board TIROS-N, NOAA-06 to NOAA-19, Metop-A, and Metop-B.

The polygons, required for the data tailoring, show problems with non-continues data. Some polygons of the HIRS data record are found to be incorrect. However, this does not affect the correctness of the data itself. _source.abstract:
This is a reprocessed level 3 (L3) dataset at DT-2024 baseline, which covers from 29 December 2021 to 31 December 2023. The L3 LR products contain global valid 1Hz subsampled along-track sea level anomaly multi-mission intercalibrated (orbit error and long wave-length error) over water, based on LR level 2p products.

The reference mission used for the altimeter inter-calibration processing is:
- Topex/Poseidon: 01-01-1993 to 23-04-2002
- Jason-1: 24-04-2002 to 18-10-2008
- OSTM/Jason-2: 19-10-2008 to 25-06-2016
- Jason-3: 25-06-2016 to 09-02-2022
- Sentinel-6A: from 10-02-2022

These products are suitable for users seeking information on downstream sea level added value products. Sentinel-6 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme. It is a collaborative Copernicus mission, implemented and co-funded by the European Commission, ESA, EUMETSAT and the USA, through NASA and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

_source.abstract:
EUMETSAT has funded studies for developing Total Column Water Vapour (TCWV) retrievals from the OLCI instrument. Although the primary focus of OLCI is on ocean and land, the atmosphere has become important user driven application, both for atmospheric correction and deriving stand-alone dedicated atmospheric products. These developments have resulted in the TCWV product, also known as COWa (Copernicus Sentinel-3 OLCI Water vapour). The algorithm uses a 1D-Var optimal estimation scheme and multiple spectral bands around 0.9 microns.

The output is produced in cloud-free daytime only, with a known higher information content above land (bright surface signal).

Water vapour (H₂O) in the atmosphere is a key component of the Earth’s hydrological cycle, critical in shaping the global environment and supporting life on Earth as we know it.

Manifold physical processes thereby help redistributing the water from the oceans to the land involving the formation of clouds, precipitation, and extreme weather events. Water vapour also has a key role in constraining the Earth’s energy balance. It is the single most important natural greenhouse gas in the atmosphere and constitutes a strong positive feedback to anthropogenic climate forcing from carbon dioxide (CO₂).

The water vapour feedback is critically important in understanding past and determining future climate change and its global and regional impacts.

This is a dedicated and standalone Sentinel-3 level 2 Atmospheric TCWV product, directly driven by Meteorology and Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) user needs. It differs from the historical TCWV product OLCI L2 Total Columnar Water Vapour in NRT (BUFR) - Sentinel-3, based on the Integrated Water Vapour (IWV) parameter present in the OLCI L2 Marine product, and which is planned to be discontinued by 2028.

_source.abstract:
The Copernicus Sentinel-3 SLSTR level 2 Ice Surface Temperature (IST) product extends the existing marine SST portfolio to the cryosphere by providing surface skin temperature over sea-ice and water poleward of 50° latitude in both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, in both Near Real Time (NRT, < 3 hours) and Non Time Critical (NTC, <30 days) timeliness as ~3 min granules. Ice surface temperature is one of a key climate variables that influences energy exchange between the surface and atmosphere, sea-ice growth and melt processes, and the monitoring of polar climate change.

Key features include two complementary retrieval algorithms: a nadir-only split-window retrieval and a dual-view single-channel retrieval, distributed in separate NetCDF files. A unified surface temperature field combines SST, IST, or a weighted mixture depending on surface type. Cloud screening is based on the EUMETSAT NWC SAF Polar Platform System (PPS) cloud products, while auxiliary sea-ice concentration data support surface classification into ocean, ice, and mixed pixels.

The product provides per-pixel quality levels, total and component uncertainties, and GHRSST-compliant metadata and file formats.

Validation against Polar weather stations and airborne observations demonstrates that quality levels 4 and 5 meet the GCOS target accuracy requirement of 3 K, with typical daytime bias and standard deviation below 2 K for both retrieval algorithms. The product is generated using the SLSTR SST/IST Instrument Processing Facility (IPF) v07.00 and establishes an operational capability for monitoring surface temperature across both polar oceans and sea-ice regions, supporting climate monitoring, numerical weather prediction, sea-ice modelling, and operational polar applications.

Ice surface temperature is one of a key climate variables that influences energy exchange between the surface and atmosphere, sea-ice growth and melt processes, and the monitoring of polar climate change.

Key features include two complementary retrieval algorithms: a nadir-only split-window retrieval and a dual-view single-channel retrieval, distributed in separate NetCDF files. A unified surface temperature field combines SST, IST, or a weighted mixture depending on surface type. Cloud screening is based on the EUMETSAT NWC SAF Polar Platform System (PPS) cloud products, while auxiliary sea-ice concentration data support surface classification into ocean, ice, and mixed pixels.

The product provides per-pixel quality levels, total and component uncertainties, and GHRSST-compliant metadata and file formats.

Validation against Polar weather stations and airborne observations demonstrates that quality levels 4 and 5 meet the GCOS target accuracy requirement of 3 K, with typical daytime bias and standard deviation below 2 K for both retrieval algorithms. The product is generated using the SLSTR SST/IST Instrument Processing Facility (IPF) v07.00 and establishes an operational capability for monitoring surface temperature across both polar oceans and sea-ice regions, supporting climate monitoring, numerical weather prediction, sea-ice modelling, and operational polar applications.","identifier":"EO:EUM:DAT:1096","name":"SLSTR Level 2 Ice Surface Temperature - Sentinel-3"}

_source.abstract:
The SLSTR level 2 AMV products contain the Atmospheric Motion Vectors (AMVs) derived by tracking cloud features in the Brightness Temperature (BT) images of the nadir view in band S8. These data include the speeds, directions, heights and geographical locations of the wind vectors. These measurements are accompanied with tracking and time information, quality indexes and meteorological auxiliary data.

- All Sentinel-3 NRT products are available at pick-up point in less than 3h.
- Sentinel-3 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme.

_source.abstract:
This is a reprocessed dataset at baseline F08, which is continued by the NTC data stream from 09/Feb/2023 onwards. The level 1a product contains level 1 intermediate output of the HR processor (RAW and RMC). It includes geo-located bursts of Ku echoes (at ~9 kHz) with all instrument calibrations applied. It includes the full rate complex waveforms input to the delay/Doppler or SAR processor. This product is most relevant to altimetry specialists, working on fundamental SAR processing techniques and calibration studies.

Sentinel-6 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme. It is a collaborative Copernicus mission, implemented and co-funded by the European Commission, ESA, EUMETSAT and the USA, through NASA and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

_source.abstract:
The RINEX dataset is a supplementary dataset to the Release 1, 2 and 3 - GRAS level 1b Bending Angle FCDRs. The RINEX files contain pseudorange, carrier phase, and amplitude/SNR data of the zenith antenna, and are formatted in standard RINEX v2.10 observation format. One RINEX file is available per day, with a file size of approximately 65 MB per file.

The approximate size of the complete RINEX data record is:
- about 415 GB for Metop-A
- 237 GB for Metop-B
- 50 GB for Metop-C

This is a Fundamental Climate Data Record (FCDR).

_source.abstract:
This product is an RGB composite based upon data from Sentinel-3 OLCI level 1b NRT top of atmosphere (TOA) radiances from bands 0a08_radiance (Red), Oa06_radiance (Green) and Oa03_radiance (Blue), corrected for Rayleigh scattering and solar path length.

The primary objective of Sentinel-3 OLCI is to measure the colour of the ocean and land surface and provide information on ocean and land characteristics related to this (e.g. biology). OLCI also provides information on atmospheric composition and contributes to climate studies. This layer accentuates ocean colour; the change in the colour of the ocean, and other water bodies such as lakes, due to the substances dissolved and particles suspended within the water.

The images are generated with a pixel resolution of 0.06 degrees. Each step in the layer shows an individual orbit for Sentinel-3B. This layer can be exported from EUMETView as an via the Web Map Service (WMS).

Sentinel-3 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme.

_source.abstract:
Medium Resolution Sea Ice Drift product covers the Northern Hemisphere (NH) above 40 Deg. N. Ice motion vectors with a time span of approximately 24 hours are estimated by a maximum cross-correlation method (MCC) on pairs of satellite images. The ice drift product is based on swath data from the AVHRR instrument onboard the Metop-A satellite.
- VISible data are used to determine ice motion during summer (MJJA).
- Thermal InfraRed data are used from September to April.

Valid drift data are only available in cloud free areas, due to cloud opacity of VIS and TIR data. Data from 19 May 2025 onwards can only be accessed from the SAF Archive.

_source.abstract:
This Climate Data Record (CDR) provides the Surface Radiation Budget, Latent and Sensible Heat Fluxes derived from the Meteosat Visible and InfraRed Imager (MVIRI) on board the Meteosat First Generation (MFG) and the Spinning Enhanced Visible and InfraRed Imager (SEVIRI) onboard the Meteosat Second Generation (MSG) satellites. The covered time period ranges from January 1983 to December 2020. Original thermal radiances were inter-calibrated by the European Organisation for the Exploitation of Meteorological Satellites (EUMETSAT).

The single radiation components of the surface radiation budget (SRB) are derived from the thermal and optical channels of the MVIRI and SEVIRI instruments onboard the geostationary Meteosat satellites. All components of the SRB are derived jointly based on physical retrieval schemes using the GeoSatClim software. Surface Latent and Sensible Heat fluxes are obtained thanks to an adapted version of the land surface model developed by the Satellite Application Facility on Land Surface Analysis (LSA SAF). While soil moisture and meteorological inputs are adapted from ERA5 dataset, the radiation components of the surface radiation budget described above are taken as model input. This is a Thematic Climate Data Record (TCDR).

_source.abstract:
This product is an RGB composite based upon data from Sentinel-3 OLCI level 1b NRT top of atmosphere (TOA) radiances from bands 0a08_radiance (Red), Oa06_radiance (Green) and Oa03_radiance (Blue), corrected for Rayleigh scattering and solar path length.

The primary objective of Sentinel-3 OLCI is to measure the colour of the ocean and land surface and provide information on ocean and land characteristics related to this (e.g. biology). OLCI also provides information on atmospheric composition and contributes to climate studies. This layer accentuates ocean colour; the change in the colour of the ocean, and other water bodies such as lakes, due to the substances dissolved and particles suspended within the water.

The images are generated with a pixel resolution of 0.06 degrees. Each step in the layer incrementally accumulates product of all the orbits over an entire day from both Sentinel-3A and Sentinel-3B.

Sentinel-3 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme.

_source.abstract:
IASI-NG, a passive infrared sounder, measures temperature and water vapour profiles of the Earth’s atmosphere. IASI-NG also has a huge potential to measure greenhouse gases, clouds, aerosols, ozone, and trace gases.

A scan line is made of 14 fields of regard (FOR) consisting of 4X4 instantaneous and individual fields of view (FOV), with each FOV having a 12km ground resolution.

IASI-NG level 1c product provides calibrated radiance and geolocated radiance emitted by the Earth over 16921 spectral samples between 645.0 cm-1 and 2760 cm-1 (15.5 µm and 3.63 µm) in four contiguous bands. The raw spectra received from the instrument are rendered independent of the instrument SRF effects by applying a so-called “ISRF removal” i.e. a correction of the effects of the instrument self-apodisation.

_source.abstract:
The WSFM01 SDR product provides near real-time native Sensor Data Record (SDR) observations from the Microwave Imager (MWI) aboard the Weather System Follow-on Microwave (WSF-M1) satellite.

Supplied by NOAA and redistributed by EUMETSAT in its native netCDF format, this dataset is the international equivalent of a standard level 1b (L1b) product. It is specifically designed to support advanced meteorological, oceanographic, and environmental monitoring applications.

_source.abstract:
This ASCAT Multi-parameter product contains surface wind vectors over ocean and soil moisture index over land. Additionally, the backscatter values involved in the retrieval of the geophysical parameters above are also included, as well as several quality flags to facilitate the use of the data. For NWP users this product is provided in BUFR format. The netCDF version of this product contains Winds ONLY.

For users interested in either ASCAT backscatter, wind or soil moisture index data in other formats, please refer to the relevant product entries available for the specific parameters. Finally, note that although the OSI SAF is identified as the originating centre for this product, it is not responsible for the processing of soil moisture index values, which is currently carried out at EUMETSAT.

For wind data before 1 April 2014: better than using this archived NRT product, please use the reprocessed ASCAT winds data records (EO:EUM:DAT:Metop:OSI-150-A, EO:EUM:DAT:Metop:OSI-150-B). Metop-A data are available in the Data Centre up to 15/11/2021.

_source.abstract:
Local mission data from Metop-SG instruments is broadcast in real time by the satellites to receiving stations in the visibility of the satellite ('direct broadcast'). The transmission of local mission data is in X-Band, and the raw data from the satellite is received at the reception station with a 3-meter antenna. The reception stations are equipped with level 0 and level 1 processing software which generate L1 products from the raw data. EUMETSAT provides the L0 processing software for all Metop-SG instruments and L1 processing software for IASI-NG, MWS, METimage, MWI, ICI and SCA instruments. The software is available from the NWP SAF website.
 METimage is a multi-spectral (visible and IR) imaging passive radiometer which provides detailed information on clouds, wind, aerosols and surface properties, which are essential for meteorological and climate applications. The primary objective of the mission is to provide high quality imagery data for global and regional numerical weather prediction (NWP), nowcasting, and climate monitoring, by providing information on:

- High horizontal resolution cloud products, including microphysical analysis,
- Sea surface temperature,
- Vegetation, snow coverage, and fire monitoring products,
- Aerosol products,
- Polar atmospheric motion vectors.

The mission objectives also include providing information on aerosols, cloud size, surface albedo, fire, land and ice surface temperature, snow cover, and soil moisture. An important objective of METimage is to support the sounders onboard the Metop-SG A satellite, for their geolocation, cloud characterisation, and scene inhomogeneity quantification for correction of the spectral response.

_source.abstract:
Release 1 of the Climate Data Record (CDR) of MSG imager SEVIRI (Spinning Enhanced Visible Infra-Red Imager) Atmospheric Motion Vectors (AMV) located at the 0° position. This release covers the MSG SEVIRI record from four different satellite platforms Meteosat-8 to -11. The CDR covers 15 years from 19 January 2004 until 31 August 2019 and there is a hourly products in netCDF format.

It provides information on AMV speed (ms-1), direction (degree), and height (given in pressure units Pa) of vectors which are derived by tracking cloud or water vapour features between two images in time. The vectors height is derived using the OCA cloud properties (DOI:10.15770/EUM_SEC_CLM_0049). AMV are wind vectors retrieved at all heights below the tropopause, derived from the following channels:

- Visible 0.6 microns
- Water Vapour 6.2 microns and 7.3 microns
- Infrared 10.8 microns

The data record has been generated using the standalone version of the operational software used for SEVIRI in the EUMETSAT operational level 2 Meteosat Product Extraction Facility (MPEF) and it is fully described in (MSG Meteorological Products Extraction Facility Algorithm Specification Document - EUM/MSG/SPE/022 v7B).

_source.abstract:
This dataset contains the MTG IRS-based level 1 spectral radiances represented in compressed form as the 300 leading Principal Components (PC). These are calculated from the original spectral sounding samples (SSS) making use of the high degree of correlation between the spectral channels. This correlation means the number of independent pieces of information within the 1953 (LWIR: 877, MWIR 1076) spectral channels of IRS is much smaller than the total number of samples. For any given dimension, the optimal subspace (in the sense of minimising the average norm of the orthogonal complement) is spanned by the leading Principal Components [PCA], ie, the leading eigenvectors of the (noise normalised) covariance matrix of the data. Each radiance can, therefore, be compressed into principal components scores (PCS) with minimal loss of information (mostly noise). The original radiances can be reconstructed from the Principal Components using the eigenvector basis, available from the IRS L1 data guide. Sampling the Earth disc is divided into four LACs (Local Area Coverage) regions, numbered 1 to 4 from South to North. LACn is encoded in the filename as ‘Qn’, ie, ‘Q4’ for ‘LAC4’ etc. LAC4 covering Europe is scanned every 30 minutes, and LACs 1, 2 and 3 are scanned in a different sequence.

This catalogue entry covers LAC4 hourly data (hourly: LAC4 scan ending at the full hour), which are classified as Core data as per EUMETSAT Data Policy.

_source.abstract:
The second edition of the CM SAF Upper Tropospheric Humidity (UTH) is a satellite-based climate data record. It is a near-global 1°x1° latitude-longitude dataset that is produced with both hourly and daily time steps. The dataset is based on data from twelve passive microwave (MW) sounders operating at 183 GHz in polar orbit that are combined into a single time series covering the period 6 July 1994 to 31 December 2018. The UTH provided typically represents a broad atmospheric layer between 500 and 200 hPa. However, the exact height of this layer depends on the atmospheric conditions at the time of the observation.

An optional fixed layer approximation adjustment is supplied that users can apply to provide an estimated mean relative humidity (RH) between ±60° latitude for a fixed layer between 500 and 200 hPa (mean_RH). However, users are advised to take care using this correction, especially outside of the tropics where the mean_RH is of lower quality. Users are also advised to take care using UTH observations above ±60° latitude as the retrieval is sometimes less reliable at high latitudes.

Further information describing the dataset in detail can be found in the available product documentation. This is a Thematic Climate Data Record (TCDR).

_source.abstract:
The TOOCAN database is a level 2 product of Deep Convective Cloud Systems (DCS) parameters derived from Meteosat measurements. Fundamental Climate Data Records of Meteosat First and Second Generation instruments MVIRI and SEVIRI (John et al., 2019) are used as input for the TOOCAN (Fiolleau and Roca 2013) cloud tracking algorithm to detect and track DCS from the geostationary infrared observations.

TOOCAN data provides integrated morphological parameters of tropical DCS such as:
- Location and time of initiation and dissipation
- Lifetime duration
- Propagated distance
- Maximum extent

The data are available for region with boundaries 40° S to 40° N and 55° W to 55° E for the 1981-2023 period. The data has been used to reveal changes in convective organisation over tropical Africa and Atlantic Ocean (Rocal et al., 2024).

The TOOCAN database is composed by two types of files:
Regional segmented images at a 0.04° spatial resolution and a 30-minute temporal frequency (in netCDF).
Regional and monthly tracking files (in ASCII and in netCDF) documenting the DCS morphological parameters at each 30 minute-step of their life cycles.

Each DCS is then described by a unique label, which is useful for making the link between a given DCS described in the tracking files and the same DCS identified in the segmented images. Thus, using both the tracking file and the segmented images provides access to all the pixels of a given DCS identified in the segmented images, as well as to its morphological parameters in the monthly tracking files.

TOOCAN data provides integrated morphological parameters of tropical DCS such as:
- Location and time of initiation and dissipation
- Lifetime duration
- Propagated distance
- Maximum extent

The TOOCAN database is composed by two types of files:
Regional segmented images at a 0.04° spatial resolution and a 30-minute temporal frequency (in netCDF).
Regional and monthly tracking files (in ASCII and in netCDF) documenting the DCS morphological parameters at each 30 minute-step of their life cycles.

_source.abstract:
Customised Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) FCI level 1c and level 2 data disseminated via EUMETCast Africa, which form the MTG Africa data service. Due to the limited bandwidth on EUMETCast Africa, the MTG data needs to be tailored in order to provide the best fit for the needs of the African user community.

The MTG Africa data service disseminated via EUMETCast Africa provides a subset of MTG data derived from the FCI Full Disc Scanning Service (FDSS). The service comprises:
- Tailored FCI L1c data, 16 bands in 3 km and one band in 1 km resolution (netCDF4) (original, uncustomised data in full spatial and temporal resolution: EO:EUM:DAT:0662)
- Centrally generated and tailored RGBs: Severe Convection, Night Microphysics, True Colour, Fire Temperature and Cloud Phase (GeoTIFF)
- A selection of tailored L2 data from EUMETSAT's central facility and SAFs, currently only GII (original, uncustomised data in full spatial and temporal resolution: EO:EUM:DAT:0683)

Some uncustomised MTG data are also available in the EUMETCast Africa Service, such as LI L2 and FCI L2 central facility and SAF products.

_source.abstract:
The GIRAFE v1 climate data record (CDR) provides precipitation estimates derived from a combination of passive microwave (PMW) observations onboard polar orbiting satellites and infrared (IR) observations onboard geostationary satellites. The GIRAFE v1 CDR covers the time period 2002/01/01 until 2022/12/31 and is extended to the present day by the GIRAFE v1 Interim CDR from 2023/01/01 with a latency of 10 days to three months.

The PMW input to GIRAFE v1 is from various microwave imager and sounder instruments. Precipitation rate estimates are retrieved from the observed PMW brightness temperatures by precipitation retrieval algorithms HOAPS, PNPR-CLIM (*1), and PRPS. The resulting archives of instantaneous precipitation rate estimates are homogenized using quantile mapping.

The IR input to GIRAFE comes from the five geostationary positions forming the Geo-Ring, providing observations along all geographical longitudes. The spatially and temporally highly resolved IR input is trained to detect the occurrence of precipitation using the PMW-based instantaneous precipitation rate estimates. Conditional precipitation rates are computed based on PMW observations only. At latitudes higher than 55°N/S where Geo-Ring IR pixels are extremely distorted, GIRAFE v1 relies only on the PMW input.

GIRAFE v1 is a gridded product which is available globally at a spatial resolution of 1° x 1° and at a temporal resolution of 24 h as accumulated precipitation computed from the (IR-based) fraction of precipitation and the conditional precipitation rate. Additionally, 1° x 1° monthly mean values of the daily accumulated precipitation are provided.

The daily accumulated precipitation features a dedicated sampling uncertainty at the same 1° x 1° x 24 h resolution which is based on the analysis of decorrelation scales in space and time in the IR-based precipitation fields.

(*1) The PNPR-CLIM algorithm has been developed by CNR-ISAC in the C3S_312b_Lot1 Copernicus project.

The GIRAFE v1 CDR covers the time period 2002/01/01 until 2022/12/31 and is extended to the present day by the GIRAFE v1 Interim CDR from 2023/01/01 with a latency of 10 days to three months.

The PMW input to GIRAFE v1 is from various microwave imager and sounder instruments. Precipitation rate estimates are retrieved from the observed PMW brightness temperatures by precipitation retrieval algorithms HOAPS, PNPR-CLIM (*1), and PRPS. The resulting archives of instantaneous precipitation rate estimates are homogenized using quantile mapping.

The IR input to GIRAFE comes from the five geostationary positions forming the Geo-Ring, providing observations along all geographical longitudes. The spatially and temporally highly resolved IR input is trained to detect the occurrence of precipitation using the PMW-based instantaneous precipitation rate estimates. Conditional precipitation rates are computed based on PMW observations only. At latitudes higher than 55°N/S where Geo-Ring IR pixels are extremely distorted, GIRAFE v1 relies only on the PMW input.

GIRAFE v1 is a gridded product which is available globally at a spatial resolution of 1° x 1° and at a temporal resolution of 24 h as accumulated precipitation computed from the (IR-based) fraction of precipitation and the conditional precipitation rate. Additionally, 1° x 1° monthly mean values of the daily accumulated precipitation are provided.

The daily accumulated precipitation features a dedicated sampling uncertainty at the same 1° x 1° x 24 h resolution which is based on the analysis of decorrelation scales in space and time in the IR-based precipitation fields.

(*1) The PNPR-CLIM algorithm has been developed by CNR-ISAC in the C3S_312b_Lot1 Copernicus project.","identifier":"EO:EUM:DAT:0921","name":"GIRAFE v1: CM SAF Global Interpolated RAinFall Estimation version 1"}

_source.abstract:
This product is an operational extension of the Sea Ice Concentration Climate Data Record OSI-450 (See resource link below), with a latency of 16 days, starting in 2016. OSI-430-b uses passive microwave data (PMW) from the SSMIS sensors, and the same algorithms as OSI-450. The product includes error-bars for each grid cell (uncertainties). 

Note: This product has been discontinued, release 3 (10.15770/EUM_SAF_OSI_0014) of this ICDR should be used. Also release 3.1 (10.15770/EUM_SAF_OSI_0023) of the CDR should be used.

_source.abstract:
The glyoxal data record provides long-term information about vertical column densities of CHOCHO in the atmosphere. The retrieval of the product is based on GOME-2 radiance measurements in the wavelength region 405-490 nm. CHOCHO columns are given as densities (molecules/cm2). Glyoxal is an organic compound with the chemical formula C2H2O2.

The temporal coverage for Metop-A and B is as follows:
- Metop-A: 23/01/2007 - 31/12/2017
- Metop-B: 01/01/2013 - 30/06/2020

_source.abstract:
This dataset contains the MTG IRS level 1 spectral radiances in [W/m2/sr/m-1], provided as 877 ‘spectral sounding samples’ (SSS) in the long-wave IR range (LWIR), and 1076 samples in the mid-wave IR range (MWIR). A dwell consisting of 160x160 pixels represents a data cube of 160x160x(877+1076) values. Sampling the Earth disc is divided into four LACs (Local Area Coverage) regions, numbered 1 to 4 from South to North. LACn is encoded in the filename as ‘Qn’, ie, ‘Q4’ for ‘LAC4’ etc. LAC4 covering Europe is scanned every 30 minutes, and LACs 1, 2 and 3 are scanned in a different sequence.

This catalogue entry covers all data from LAC1, 2 and 3 as well as non-hourly data from LAC4. These data are classified as Recommended data as per EUMETSAT Data Policy.

_source.abstract:
The Fire Radiative Power product (FRP, in megawatts) provides information on the measured radiant heat output of detected fires. It has been demonstrated in small-scale experimental fires that the amount of radiant heat energy liberated per unit time (the Fire Radiative Power) is related to the rate at which fuel is being consumed. This is a direct result of the combustion process, whereby carbon-based fuel is oxidised to CO2 with the release of a certain heat yield. Therefore, measuring this FRP and integrating it over the lifetime of the fire provides an estimate of the total Fire Radiative Energy (FRE), which for wildfires should be proportional to the total mass of fuel biomass combusted.

Geostationary observations allow high temporal frequency FRP measurements, and thus a much-improved ability to estimate FRE via temporal integration when compared to the far less-frequent observations made from systems in low-Earth orbit. The FRP product is derived every 10 min at the High Resolution of the MTG FCI sensor (1km). The product includes for each processed pixel:

- FRP (MW)
- Corresponding uncertainty in the FRP retrieval based on the variability of the background radiance estimation
- A confidence measure (representing the level of confidence that the observation is indeed a true fire)

Applications: The FRP product is intended to support emerging operational atmosphere, climate and climatewildfire management-related applications, such as air quality forecasting, carbon cycle assessment and modelling, and fire activity models.

_source.abstract:
This ocean colour product represents the algal pigment (chlorophyll a) concentration in clear open waters.

- Prior to the introduction of baseline collection 004 (BC004) on February 25, 2026, the algal pigment concentration (chl_oc4me) layer was defined by the OC4ME maximum band ratio (MBR) semi-analytical algorithm. The product is log10 scaled. The following flags were applied: CLOUD, CLOUD_AMBIGUOUS, CLOUD_MARGIN, INVALID, COSMETIC, SATURATED, SUSPECT, HISOLZEN, HIGHGLINT, SNOW_ICE, AC_FAIL, WHITECAPS, ADJAC, RWNEG_O2, RWNEG_O3, RWNEG_O4, RWNEG_O5, RWNEG_O6, RWNEG_O7, RWNEG_O8, OC4ME_FAIL. Full details of the chl_oc4me algorithm can be found in the resource links. The product was derived using the Sentinel-3 OLCI NRT level 2 water-leaving reflectances (calculated from the Baseline Atmospheric Correction, BAC).
- Since the introduction of BC004, the algal pigment concentration layer (chlor_a) is defined using a blending approach based on optical water classes, with a chlorophyll index (CI) for ultra‑oligotrophic, the OC4 algorithm for oligotrophic, Multiple band ratio (MBR) for mesotrophic, and an NDCI‑based model for turbid waters. The product is log10 scaled. The following flags were applied: CLOUD, CLOUD_AMBIGUOUS, CLOUD_MARGIN, INVALID, COSMETIC, SATURATED, SUSPECT, HISOLZEN, UNCORR_GLINT, SNOW_ICE, AC_FAIL, WHITECAPS, ADJAC, RWNEG_O2, RWNEG_O3, RWNEG_O4, RWNEG_O5, RWNEG_O6, RWNEG_O7, RWNEG_O8, CHLOR_A_FAIL. Full details of the chlor_a algorithm can be found in the resource links. The product was derived using the Sentinel-3 OLCI NRT L2 remote sensing reflectances (calculated from the Ocean Colour Standard Atmospheric Correction, OC-SAC).

Each step in the layer incrementally accumulates product of all the orbits over an entire day from both Sentinel-3A and Sentinel-3B. This product can be downloaded as numerical data in EUMETView via the Web Coverage Service (WCS).

Sentinel-3 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme.

_source.abstract:
The Meteosat Data Collection Service (DCS), currently supported by Meteosat at 0° and IODC, is one of the core services operated by EUMETSAT in support of meteorology and weather prediction. The service enables Data Collection Platform (DCP) Operators to use the Meteosat system to relay environmental data collected from DCP platforms equipped with certified DCP Transmitters.

A Data Collection Platform (DCP) can be any measurement facility (eg, an automatic weather station or an ocean buoy) which collects environmental data through instruments/sensors. The instruments/sensors can measure different environmental parameters, such as wind speed, direction, rainfall, water level, temperature, seismic activity, fire index parameters, etc. The DCP Transmitter allows for the automatic retrieval of data from the DCP, which can be particularly advantageous for data collection in remote or inhospitable locations where it may provide the only possibility for data relay.

The EUMETSAT DCS currently supports both standard-rate (100bps) and high-rate (1200bps) DCPs. EUMETSAT no longer assigns new standard-rate (100 bps) DCPs. The high-rate (HRDCP) has improved capabilities and can be used for applications such as warnings of potentially devastating natural phenomena such as tsunamis.

DCP data re-transmitted via the Meteosat satellites are routed for onward delivery to users via:
- EUMETCast
- The DCS Web Service
- The Global Telecommunication System (GTS) community

_source.abstract:
This Climate Data Record (CDR) provides Land Surface Temperature (LST) derived from the Meteosat Visible and InfraRed Imager (MVIRI) on board the Meteosat First Generation (MFG) and the Spinning Enhanced Visible and InfraRed Imager (SEVIRI) onboard the Meteosat Second Generation (MSG) satellites. The covered time period ranges from January 1983 to December 2020. Original thermal radiances were inter-calibrated by the European Organisation for the Exploitation of Meteorological Satellites (EUMETSAT).

The LST is derived from Meteosat by use of single-channel LST retrieval based on radiative transfer calculations. The LST is presented as hourly data and as monthly averaged diurnal cycle composites on a 0.05°x0.05° grid covering the Meteosat disk (Africa and Europe). A summary of the retrieval algorithms is provided by Duguay–Tetzlaff et al. 2015. This is a Thematic Climate Data Record (TCDR).

_source.abstract:
Stress-equivalent 10m winds over the global oceans obtained from the ScatSat-1 OSCAT scatterometer are derived from radar backscatter measurements. The ScatSat-1 satellite, launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), carries an Oceansat-2 Scatterometer (OSCAT) instrument that measures normalized radar cross-section at Ku-band frequency. These backscatter measurements are sensitive to centimeter-scale roughness on the ocean surface, which is directly related to surface wind stress.

The stress-equivalent wind represents the wind speed that would produce the observed surface stress under neutral atmospheric stability conditions at a reference height of 10 meters above the sea surface. This differs from the actual wind speed because the relationship between wind and stress depends on atmospheric stability. The stress-equivalent formulation is preferred for oceanographic applications because:

- It provides a more direct measure of momentum transfer from atmosphere to ocean
- It reduces errors associated with stability corrections
- It is more consistent with ocean model forcing requirements

The ScatSat-1 OSCAT data processing involves several steps:

- Geophysical Model Function application to convert backscatter to wind vectors
- Quality control to remove contaminated observations (rain, ice, land)
- Wind direction ambiguity removal using numerical weather prediction models
- Conversion to stress-equivalent winds using bulk flux algorithms

The resulting wind products typically have:

- Spatial resolution of 25-50 km
- Wind speed accuracy of approximately 1-2 m/s
- Wind direction accuracy of approximately 20 degrees
- Global coverage every 2 days at the equator, with improved coverage at higher latitudes

These stress-equivalent winds are particularly valuable for ocean circulation studies, air-sea interaction research, and operational ocean forecasting systems.

_source.abstract:
This ocean colour product represents the algal pigment (chlorophyll a) concentration in clear open waters.

- Prior to the introduction of baseline collection 004 (BC004) on February 25, 2026, the algal pigment concentration (chl_oc4me) layer was defined by the OC4ME maximum band ratio (MBR) semi-analytical algorithm. The product is log10 scaled. The following flags were applied: CLOUD, CLOUD_AMBIGUOUS, CLOUD_MARGIN, INVALID, COSMETIC, SATURATED, SUSPECT, HISOLZEN, HIGHGLINT, SNOW_ICE, AC_FAIL, WHITECAPS, ADJAC, RWNEG_O2, RWNEG_O3, RWNEG_O4, RWNEG_O5, RWNEG_O6, RWNEG_O7, RWNEG_O8, OC4ME_FAIL. Full details of the chl_oc4me algorithm can be found in the resource links. The product was derived using the Sentinel-3A OLCI NRT level 2 water-leaving reflectances (calculated from the Baseline Atmospheric Correction, BAC).
- Since the introduction of BC004, the algal pigment concentration layer (chlor_a) is defined using a blending approach based on optical water classes, with a chlorophyll index (CI) for ultra‑oligotrophic, the OC4 algorithm for oligotrophic, Multiple band ratio (MBR) for mesotrophic, and an NDCI‑based model for turbid waters. The product is log10 scaled. The following flags were applied: CLOUD, CLOUD_AMBIGUOUS, CLOUD_MARGIN, INVALID, COSMETIC, SATURATED, SUSPECT, HISOLZEN, UNCORR_GLINT, SNOW_ICE, AC_FAIL, WHITECAPS, ADJAC, RWNEG_O2, RWNEG_O3, RWNEG_O4, RWNEG_O5, RWNEG_O6, RWNEG_O7, RWNEG_O8, CHLOR_A_FAIL. Full details of the chlor_a algorithm can be found in the resource links. The product was derived using the Sentinel-3A OLCI NRT L2 remote sensing reflectances (calculated from the Ocean Colour Standard Atmospheric Correction, OC-SAC).

Each step in the layer shows an individual orbit for Sentinel-3A. This product can be downloaded as numerical data in EUMETView via the Web Coverage Service (WCS).

Sentinel-3 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme.

_source.abstract:
OLCI (Ocean and Land Colour Instrument) NRT and NTC level 1b products at reduced resolution (1200m at nadir). L1b products include the following:

- top of atmosphere radiances in 21 bands, Oa??_radiance (400, 412, 442, 490, 510, 560, 620, 665, 674, 681, 709, 754, 761, 764, 767, 779, 865, 885, 900, 940, 1024 nm);

Calibrated TOA radiance values are calculated from instrument numerical counts, corrected for non-linearity, dark signal, smear and absolute gain calibration, prior to cosmetic pixel filling, stray-light correction and geo-referencing. Radiances and associated uncertainties are provided on a resampled output grid, alongside initial pixel classifications. Auxiliary meteorological data, geolocation data and acquisition geometry are provided on tie points grids.

- All Sentinel-3 NRT products are available at pick-up point in less than 3h
- All Sentinel-3 Non Time Critical (NTC) products are available at pick-up point in less than 30 days.

Sentinel-3 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme.

_source.abstract:
This is a reprocessed dataset at baseline F06, which is continued by the NRT/NTC data stream from 29/April/2022 onwards. The level 1a product contains level 1 intermediate output of the HR processor (RAW and RMC). It includes geo-located bursts of Ku echoes (at ~9 kHz) with all instrument calibrations applied. It includes the full rate complex waveforms input to the delay/Doppler or SAR processor. This product is most relevant to altimetry specialists, working on fundamental SAR processing techniques and calibration studies.

Sentinel-6 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme. It is a collaborative Copernicus mission, implemented and co-funded by the European Commission, ESA, EUMETSAT and the USA, through NASA and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

_source.abstract:
The level 2 low resolution (LR) product is output of the LR L2 processor. It contains the altimeter range, the sea surface height, the wind speed, significant wave height and all required geophysical corrections and related flags derived from the LR processor.

Two measurement data files are available (standard and reduced), each with a different number of variables:
- The standard data file includes 1 Hz and 20 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz and some at 20 Hz.
- The reduced data file contains only 1 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz.

Processed in NRT (< 3 hours), STC (< 36 hours) and in NTC (< 60 days).

The level 2 low resolution (LR) product is output of the LR L2 processor. It contains the altimeter range, the sea surface height, the wind speed, significant wave height and all required geophysical corrections and related flags derived from the LR processor.

Two measurement data files are available (standard and reduced), each with a different number of variables:
- The **standard** data file includes 1 Hz and 20 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz and some at 20 Hz.
- The **reduced** data file contains only 1 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz.

Processed in NRT (< 3 hours), STC (< 36 hours) and in NTC (< 60 days).

$schema ./collection_schema_v2-15.json hierarchyLevel series collectionType Dataset abstract The level 2 low resolution (LR) product is output of the LR L2 processor. It contains the altimeter range, the sea surface height, the wind speed, significant wave height and all required geophysical corrections and related flags derived from the LR processor.

Two measurement data files are available (standard and reduced), each with a different number of variables:
- The standard data file includes 1 Hz and 20 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz and some at 20 Hz.
- The reduced data file contains only 1 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz.

Processed in NRT (< 3 hours), STC (< 36 hours) and in NTC (< 60 days). abstractFormatted The level 2 low resolution (LR) product is output of the LR L2 processor. It contains the altimeter range, the sea surface height, the wind speed, significant wave height and all required geophysical corrections and related flags derived from the LR processor.

Two measurement data files are available (standard and reduced), each with a different number of variables:
- The **standard** data file includes 1 Hz and 20 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz and some at 20 Hz.
- The **reduced** data file contains only 1 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz.

Processed in NRT (< 3 hours), STC (< 36 hours) and in NTC (< 60 days).

_source.abstract:
The Sea Ice Type product is a classification product (multiyear ice/first-year ice) and covers both the Northern Hemisphere (NH) and Southern Hemisphere (SH). The sea ice type is derived from passive microwave and active microwave sensors using a multi sensor method with a Bayesian approach to combine the different sensors.

At present, it is not possible to do an ice type classification during summer from the processed channels. Accordingly:
- NH ice type product files distributed between mid-May and 30 September do not contain any valid classification.
- For the SH, no ice type classification has been defined and SH product files do not contain valid classification.

_source.abstract:
The CM SAF FCDR of Microwave Imager Radiances comprises inter-calibrated brightness temperatures (BTRs) from the SMMR, SSM/I and SSMIS radiometers. This 4th edition covers the time period from October 1978 to December 2020 including all available data from:
- the SMMR radiometer aboard Nimbus–7
- the SSM/I radiometers aboard F08, F10, F11, F13, F14, and F15
- the SSMIS radiometers aboard F16, F17, and F18

This data record has been extended by two more years of SSMIS data in December 2023. This prolongs the end of the covered time period to December 2022. The FCDR provides homogenised and inter-calibrated BTRs in a user-friendly data format. SMMR, SSM/I and SSMIS data are used for a variety of applications, such as analyses of the hydrological cycle and remote sensing of sea ice. The improved homogenization and inter-calibration procedure ensure the long term stability of the FCDR for climate related applications.

All available raw data records have been reprocessed to a common standard, starting with the calibration of the raw Earth counts, to ensure a completely homogenized data record. The data processing accounts for several known issues with the instruments and corrects calibration anomalies due to:
- along-scan inhomogeneity
- moonlight intrusions
- sunlight intrusions
- emissive reflector

Also, an adjustment to the SSMIS geolocation has been implemented in order to improve the consistency. Corrections for SMMR are limited because the SMMR raw data records were not available. Furthermore, the inter-calibration model incorporates a scene dependent inter-satellite bias correction and a non-linearity correction to the instrument calibration.

The data files contain all available original sensor data (SMMR: Pathfinder level 1b) and metadata to provide a completely traceable climate data record. Inter-calibration and Earth incidence angle normalization offsets are available as additional layers within the data files in order to keep this information transparent to the users. The data record is complemented with radiometer sensitivities, quality flags, surface types, and Earth incidence angles. This is a Fundamental Climate Data Record (FCDR).

_source.abstract:
This is a reprocessed dataset at baseline F06, which is continued by the NRT/NTC data stream from 29/April/2022 onwards. The level 1b LR product is output of the LR processor. It includes geo-located, and fully calibrated pulse-limited low-resolution Ku-band and C-band waveforms. This product is most relevant to geophysical retrieval algorithm developers (over ocean, land and ice surfaces), surface characterisations studies (eg, impact of sea state bias, wave directional effects etc) and Quality Control systems.

Sentinel-6 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme. It is a collaborative Copernicus mission, implemented and co-funded by the European Commission, ESA, EUMETSAT and the USA, through NASA and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

_source.abstract:
The FY-3F MWTS-3 BUFR product contains calibrated microwave radiance observations acquired by the Micro-Wave Temperature Sounder-3 (MWTS-3) instrument onboard the FengYun-3F polar-orbiting meteorological satellite.

The instrument measures upwelling microwave radiation in 17 channels between approximately 23.8 and 57.3 GHz, providing information on the vertical temperature structure of the atmosphere under most weather conditions. The observations support atmospheric temperature sounding, numerical weather prediction, and meteorological analysis applications.

EUMETSAT receives the source measurements in HDF format and converts them in BUFR. Both HDF and BUFR data are disseminated.

_source.abstract:
The products contain the typical altimetry measurements, like the altimeter range, the sea surface height, the wind speed, significant wave height and all required geophysical corrections and related flags. Also the sea Ice freeboard measurement is included.

The measurements in the standard data file provide the measurements in low (1 Hz = approx. 7km) and high resolution (20 Hz = approx. 300 m), in LRM mode or in SAR mode, for both C-band and Ku band. The SAR mode is the default mode. The reduced measurement data file contains 1 Hz measurements only. The enhanced measurement data file contains also the waveforms and associated parameters and the pseudo LRM measurements when in SAR mode. Sentinel-3 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme. This dataset contains reprocessed data from Baseline Collection 005, and is continued by the operational NTC data stream from 10/Mar/2023 onwards.

_source.abstract:
This Climate Data Record (CDR) provides cloud fractional cover (CFC) derived from the Meteosat Visible and InfraRed Imager (MVIRI) on board the Meteosat First Generation (MFG) and the Spinning Enhanced Visible and InfraRed Imager (SEVIRI) onboard the Meteosat Second Generation (MSG) satellites. The covered time period ranges from January 1983 to December 2020. Original thermal radiances were inter-calibrated by the European Organisation for the Exploitation of Meteorological Satellites (EUMETSAT).

The Meteosat CFC is presented as hourly, daily and monthly composites on a 0.05°x0.05° grid covering the Meteosat disk (Africa and Europe). The CFC data is derived from two Meteosat heritage channels by use of an advanced Bayesian retrieval algorithm. It employs continuous cloud scores, which are built on a contemporaneous clear sky background inversion.

The Meteosat CFC is characterised by comparability to the SYNOP-based long-term CFC observations carried out at WMO ground stations. The Meteosat CFC is therefore useful to supplement the ground-based CFC estimates in areas with low station density or high spatio-temporal CFC variability. This is a Thematic Climate Data Record (TCDR).

_source.abstract:
The GRAS-2 (GNSS Receiver for Atmospheric Sounding) level 1b data consists of vertical bending angle profiles of the atmosphere, generated for each individual occultation event. The GRAS-2 instrument on-board Metop-SG is designed to track multiple GNSS satellites, including Global Positioning Satellites (GPS), Galileo and BeiDou satellites. The tracking range up to 600 km altitude supports ionospheric sounding.

Each L1b data corresponds to a single occultation and contains the associated bending angle profile together with the lower-level data (level 1a) from which it was derived, including:
- excess-phase time series
- signal-to-noise ratios
- precise orbits and clocks for both the LEO and GNSS satellite

The L1b data in netCDF format is provided on a high resolution fixed vertical grid of impact parameter and also on a thinned resolution fixed vertical grid for both neutral atmosphere and ionosphere. The thinned version of the data is provided in BUFR format. The main applications of RO/GRAS-2 L1b data are for assimilation in NWP systems, climate, and space weather.

$schema ./collection_schema_v2-15.json hierarchyLevel series collectionType Dataset abstract The GRAS-2 (GNSS Receiver for Atmospheric Sounding) level 1b data consists of vertical bending angle profiles of the atmosphere, generated for each individual occultation event. The GRAS-2 instrument on-board Metop-SG is designed to track multiple GNSS satellites, including Global Positioning Satellites (GPS), Galileo and BeiDou satellites. The tracking range up to 600 km altitude supports ionospheric sounding.

Each L1b data corresponds to a single occultation and contains the associated bending angle profile together with the lower-level data (level 1a) from which it was derived, including:
- excess-phase time series
- signal-to-noise ratios
- precise orbits and clocks for both the LEO and GNSS satellite

The L1b data in netCDF format is provided on a high resolution fixed vertical grid of impact parameter and also on a thinned resolution fixed vertical grid for both neutral atmosphere and ionosphere. The thinned version of the data is provided in BUFR format. The main applications of RO/GRAS-2 L1b data are for assimilation in NWP systems, climate, and space weather. abstractFormatted The GRAS-2 (GNSS Receiver for Atmospheric Sounding) level 1b data consists of vertical bending angle profiles of the atmosphere, generated for each individual occultation event. _source.abstract:
The FY-3F MWHS-2 level 1 BUFR product contains calibrated microwave radiance observations acquired by the Micro-Wave Humidity Sounder-2 (MWHS-2) instrument onboard the FengYun-3F polar-orbiting meteorological satellite.

The instrument measures upwelling microwave radiation in frequency bands centred on atmospheric oxygen and water vapour absorption lines, providing information on the vertical distribution of atmospheric humidity and temperature under most weather conditions. The observations support atmospheric humidity sounding, numerical weather prediction, and meteorological analysis applications.

EUMETSAT receives the source measurements in HDF format and converts them in BUFR. Both HDF and BUFR data are disseminated.

_source.abstract:
Evapotranspiration (ET) represents the flux of water transferred from the Earth–atmosphere interface through evaporation (from soil, water bodies, and canopy interception) and transpiration by vegetation. ET is a key component of the water cycle and is associated with the latent heat flux (LE), which links the energy and water cycles. It is complemented by the sensible heat flux (MH), representing the turbulent heat exchanges at the Earth–atmosphere interface. Together, surface energy and water fluxes play a crucial role in weather forecasting, global climate monitoring, water resource management, agriculture, and ecological studies.

This product provides 30 minute ET (LSA 311.3 METv3), MLE (LSA 305.3 MLEv3), and MH (LSA 304.3 MHv3), as well as daily ET (LSA 312.3 DMETv3), obtained by integrating the 30 minute ET estimates.

The products are derived from SEVIRI observations onboard the MSG satellite, soil moisture estimates, meteorological fields, and other ancillary data, covering the period 2021 to near real time. This near real time product is consistent with and complements the Evapotranspiration and turbulent fluxes data record - MSG.

It is complemented by the sensible heat flux (MH), representing the turbulent heat exchanges at the Earth–atmosphere interface. Together, surface energy and water fluxes play a crucial role in weather forecasting, global climate monitoring, water resource management, agriculture, and ecological studies.

_source.abstract:
Leaf Area Index (LAI) is a dimensionless variable [m2/m2], which defines an important structural property of a plant canopy. LAI is defined as one-half the total leaf area per unit ground area. It accounts for the surface of leaves contained in a vertical column normalized by its cross-sectional area. It defines thus the area of green vegetation that interacts with solar radiation determining the remote sensing signal, and represents the size of the interface between the vegetation canopy and the atmosphere for energy and mass exchanges. LAI is thus a necessary input for Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP), regional and global climate modelling, weather forecasting and global change monitoring. Besides, the LAI is relevant for Land Biosphere Applications such as agriculture and forestry, environmental management and land use, hydrology, natural hazards monitoring and management, vegetation-soil dynamics monitoring and drought conditions.
This data record ETLAI-R (LSA-456) is available from January 2007 to June 2021 and is complemented and consistent with the near-real time product ETLAI (LSA-406)

This is a reprocessed dataset at baseline F06, which is continued by the NRT/NTC data stream from 29/April/2022 onwards. The level 1b HR product is output of the HR processor. It includes geo-located, and fully calibrated multi-looked high-resolution Ku-band waveforms. This product is most relevant to geophysical retrieval algorithm developers (over ocean, land and ice surfaces), surface characterisations studies (eg, impact of sea state bias, wave directional effects etc.) and Quality Control systems.

Sentinel-6 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme. It is a collaborative Copernicus mission, implemented and co-funded by the European Commission, ESA, EUMETSAT and the USA, through NASA and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

_source.abstract:
This dataset contains the MTG IRS-based level 1 spectral radiances represented in compressed form as the 300 leading Principal Components (PC). These are calculated from the original spectral sounding samples (SSS) making use of the high degree of correlation between the spectral channels. This correlation means the number of independent pieces of information within the 1953 (LWIR: 877, MWIR 1076) spectral channels of IRS is much smaller than the total number of samples. For any given dimension, the optimal subspace (in the sense of minimising the average norm of the orthogonal complement) is spanned by the leading Principal Components [PCA], ie, the leading eigenvectors of the (noise normalised) covariance matrix of the data. Each radiance can, therefore, be compressed into principal components scores (PCS) with minimal loss of information (mostly noise). The original radiances can be reconstructed from the Principal Components using the eigenvector basis, available from the IRS L1 data guide. Sampling the Earth disc is divided into four LACs (Local Area Coverage) regions, numbered 1 to 4 from South to North. LACn is encoded in the filename as ‘Qn’, ie, ‘Q4’ for ‘LAC4’ etc. LAC4 covering Europe is scanned every 30 minutes, and LACs 1, 2 and 3 are scanned in a different sequence.

This catalogue entry covers all data from LAC1, 2 and 3 as well as non-hourly data from LAC4. These data are classified as Recommended data as per EUMETSAT Data Policy.

This correlation means the number of independent pieces of information within the 1953 (LWIR: 877, MWIR 1076) spectral channels of IRS is much smaller than the total number of samples. For any given dimension, the optimal subspace (in the sense of minimising the average norm of the orthogonal complement) is spanned by the leading Principal Components [PCA], ie, the leading eigenvectors of the (noise normalised) covariance matrix of the data. Each radiance can, therefore, be compressed into principal components scores (PCS) with minimal loss of information (mostly noise). The original radiances can be reconstructed from the Principal Components using the eigenvector basis, available from the IRS L1 data guide. Sampling the Earth disc is divided into four LACs (Local Area Coverage) regions, numbered 1 to 4 from South to North. LACn is encoded in the filename as ‘Qn’, ie, ‘Q4’ for ‘LAC4’ etc. LAC4 covering Europe is scanned every 30 minutes, and LACs 1, 2 and 3 are scanned in a different sequence.

This catalogue entry covers all data from LAC1, 2 and 3 as well as non-hourly data from LAC4. _source.abstract:
Local mission data from Metop-SG instruments is broadcast in real time by the satellites to receiving stations in the visibility of the satellite ('direct broadcast'). The transmission of local mission data is in X-Band, and the raw data from the satellite is received at the reception station with a 3-meter antenna. The reception stations are equipped with level 0 and level 1 processing software which generates L1 products from the raw data. EUMETSAT provides the L0 processing software for all Metop-SG instruments and L1 processing software for IASI-NG, MWS, METimage, MWI, ICI and SCA instruments. The software is available from the NWP SAF website. 

The Microwave Sounder (MWS) is a total power radiometer which measures the brightness temperature, at various altitudes, and delivers calibrated and geo-located atmospheric temperature and water vapour sounding data. The primary objective of MWS is to support numerical weather prediction (NWP) at regional and global scales, by providing information on atmospheric temperature and water vapour profiles in clear and cloudy conditions. It also provides information on cloud liquid water columns.

_source.abstract:
The ROM SAF NRT atmosphere products are derived from measurements by the GRAS-2 radio occultation (RO) instrument onboard the Metop-SG satellite.

The RO technique utilises the bending due to refraction of GNSS radio signals as they pass through the Earth's atmosphere. Each occultation event gives a vertical profile of atmospheric refractivity, from which profiles of temperature, pressure, and humidity are retrieved. The data have a global coverage and are insensitive to clouds and the underlying surface.

The ROM SAF NRT level 2 atmosphere products include the following geophysical variables:

- Refractivity profile (GRM-130)
- Dry temperature profile (GRM-135)
- Temperature profile (GRM-131)
- Specific humidity profile (GRM-132)
- Pressure profile (GRM-133)
- Surface pressure (GRM-134)

_source.abstract:
EUMETSAT has funded studies for developing Total Column Water Vapour (TCWV) retrievals from the OLCI instrument. Although the primary focus of OLCI is on ocean and land, the atmosphere has become important user driven application, both for atmospheric correction and deriving stand-alone dedicated atmospheric products. These developments have resulted in the TCWV product, also known as COWa (Copernicus Sentinel-3 OLCI Water vapour). The algorithm uses a 1D-Var optimal estimation scheme and multiple spectral bands around 0.9 microns.

The output is produced in cloud-free daytime only, with a known higher information content above land (bright surface signal).

Water vapour (H₂O) in the atmosphere is a key component of the Earth’s hydrological cycle, critical in shaping the global environment and supporting life on Earth as we know it.

Manifold physical processes thereby help redistributing the water from the oceans to the land involving the formation of clouds, precipitation, and extreme weather events. Water vapour also has a key role in constraining the Earth’s energy balance. It is the single most important natural greenhouse gas in the atmosphere and constitutes a strong positive feedback to anthropogenic climate forcing from carbon dioxide (CO₂).

The water vapour feedback is critically important in understanding past and determining future climate change and its global and regional impacts.

This is a dedicated and standalone Sentinel-3 level 2 Atmospheric TCWV product, directly driven by Meteorology and Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) user needs. It differs from the historical TCWV product OLCI L2 Total Columnar Water Vapour in NRT (BUFR) - Sentinel-3, based on the Integrated Water Vapour (IWV) parameter present in the OLCI L2 Marine product, and which is planned to be discontinued by 2028.

_source.abstract:
The MWS level 1b radiance product consists of time-referenced, geolocated and calibrated top of the atmosphere spectral radiance measurements. The radiances are quality controlled, spectrally characterised, and annotated with satellite position and pointing. The product also contains the brightness temperatures corresponding to the radiances of all MWS channels. For each scanline, the L1b data is available for all ninety five earth view pixels.

The MWS instrument is a passive, across-track scanning radiometer capable of measuring thermal radiance emitted by the Earth and the atmosphere over twenty four spectral bands in a frequency range from 23.8 GHz to 229 GHz.

The primary role of MWS is to provide temperature and humidity atmosphere sounding. The main application of MWS L1b data is in Numerical Weather Prediction where the data is directly assimilated in NWP models. The MWS data also extends the long term climate records from microwave sounding sensors.

The data is available in BUFR format in BUFR Format Products - Metop-SG.

_source.abstract:
This is a reprocessed dataset at baseline F06, which is continued by the NRT/NTC data stream from 29/April/2022 onwards. The product contain the typical altimetry measurements, like the altimeter range, the sea surface height, the wind speed, significant wave height and all required geophysical corrections and related flags derived from LR.

Two measurement data files are available (standard and reduced), each with a different number of variables:
- The standard data file includes 1 Hz and 20 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz and some at 20 Hz.
- The reduced data file contains only 1 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz.

These products are suitable for users seeking information on sea state and those creating downstream added value products from multiple altimeters.

Sentinel-6 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme. It is a collaborative Copernicus mission, implemented and co-funded by the European Commission, ESA, EUMETSAT and the USA, through NASA and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

All Sentinel-3 Short Time Critical (STC) products are available at pick-up point in less than 48 hours. Complex (In-phase and Quadrature) echoes (I's and Q;s) after slant/Doppler range correction. This product is most relevant to geophysical retrieval algorithm developers (over ocean, land and ice surfaces), surface characterisations studies (eg, impact of sea state bias, wave directional effects etc) and Quality Control systems. Sentinel-3 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme.
- All Sentinel-3 Short Time Critical (STC) products are available at pick-up point in less than 48 hours.
- All Sentinel-3 Non Time Critical (NTC) products are available at pick-up point in less than 30 days.

_source.abstract:
This dataset contains the MTG IRS level 1 spectral radiances in [W/m2/sr/m-1], provided as 877 ‘spectral sounding samples’ (SSS) in the long-wave IR range (LWIR), and 1076 samples in the mid-wave IR range (MWIR). A dwell consisting of 160x160 pixels represents a data cube of 160x160x(877+1076) values. Sampling the Earth disc is divided into four LACs (Local Area Coverage) regions, numbered 1 to 4 from South to North. LACn is encoded in the filename as ‘Qn’, ie, ‘Q4’ for ‘LAC4’ etc. LAC4 covering Europe is scanned every 30 minutes, and LACs 1, 2 and 3 are scanned in a different sequence.

This catalogue entry covers LAC4 hourly data (hourly: LAC4 scan ending at the full hour) which are classified as Core data as per EUMETSAT Data Policy.

_source.abstract:
OLCI (Ocean and Land Colour Instrument) NRT and NTC level 1b products at full resolution (300m at nadir). L1b products include the following:

- top of atmosphere radiances in 21 bands, Oa??_radiance (400, 412, 442, 490, 510, 560, 620, 665, 674, 681, 709, 754, 761, 764, 767, 779, 865, 885, 900, 940, 1024 nm);

Calibrated TOA radiance values are calculated from instrument numerical counts, corrected for non-linearity, dark signal, smear and absolute gain calibration, prior to cosmetic pixel filling, stray-light correction and geo-referencing. Radiances and associated uncertainties are provided on a resampled output grid, alongside initial pixel classifications. Auxiliary meteorological data, geolocation data and acquisition geometry are provided on tie points grids.

- All Sentinel-3 NRT products are available at pick-up point in less than 3h
- All Sentinel-3 Non Time Critical (NTC) products are available at pick-up point in less than 30 days.

Sentinel-3 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme.

_source.abstract:
The product contain the typical altimetry measurements, like the altimeter range, the sea surface height, the wind speed, significant wave height and all required geophysical corrections and related flags derived either from RAW or RMC, or the combination of both.

Two measurement data files are available (standard and reduced), each with a different number of variables:
- The standard data file includes 1 Hz and 20 Hz measurements for the Ku- band as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz and some at 20 Hz.
- The reduced data file contains only 1 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz.

Note that the HR data products only contain Ku-band measurements. Processed in NRT (< 3 hours), STC (< 36 hours) and NTC (< 60 days).

The product contain the typical altimetry measurements, like the altimeter range, the sea surface height, the wind speed, significant wave height and all required geophysical corrections and related flags derived either from RAW or RMC, or the combination of both.

- The **standard** data file includes 1 Hz and 20 Hz measurements for the Ku- band as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz and some at 20 Hz.
- The **reduced** data file contains only 1 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz.

Note that the HR data products only contain Ku-band measurements. Processed in NRT (< 3 hours), STC (< 36 hours) and NTC (< 60 days).
