$schema ./collection_schema_v2-15.json hierarchyLevel series collectionType Dataset abstract The product contain the typical altimetry measurements, like the altimeter range, the sea surface height, the wind speed, significant wave height and all required geophysical corrections and related flags derived either from RAW or RMC, or the combination of both.

Two measurement data files are available (standard and reduced), each with a different number of variables:
- The standard data file includes 1 Hz and 20 Hz measurements for the Ku- band as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz and some at 20 Hz.
- The reduced data file contains only 1 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz.

Note that the HR data products only contain Ku-band measurements. Processed in NRT (< 3 hours), STC (< 36 hours) and NTC (< 60 days). abstractFormatted The product contain the typical altimetry measurements, like the altimeter range, the sea surface height, the wind speed, significant wave height and all required geophysical corrections and related flags derived either from RAW or RMC, or the combination of both.

Two measurement data files are available (standard and reduced), each with a different number of variables:
- The **standard** data file includes 1 Hz and 20 Hz measurements for the Ku- band as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz and some at 20 Hz.
- The **reduced** data file contains only 1 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz.

Note that the HR data products only contain Ku-band measurements. Processed in NRT (< 3 hours), STC (< 36 hours) and NTC (< 60 days).

_source.abstract:
This ASCAT Multi-parameter product contains surface wind vectors over ocean and soil moisture index over land. Additionally, the backscatter values involved in the retrieval of the geophysical parameters above are also included, as well as several quality flags to facilitate the use of the data. For NWP users this product is provided in BUFR format. The netCDF version of this product contains Winds ONLY.

For users interested in either ASCAT backscatter, wind or soil moisture index data in other formats, please refer to the relevant product entries available for the specific parameters. Finally, note that although the OSI SAF is identified as the originating centre for this product, it is not responsible for the processing of soil moisture index values, which is currently carried out at EUMETSAT.

_source.abstract:
The Copernicus NRT S3 FRP product identifies the location, and quantifies the radiative power (in MegaWatts), emitted by any hotspot present on land and ocean surfaces, that radiates a heating signal within a pixel size of 1 km2, in both daytime and nighttime conditions. All threatening hotspots are identified and characterised within 3h after SLSTR observation sensing time.

The latest Collection 3.2 of the NRT S3 FRP product (see Collection 3.2 of Sentinel-3 Near Real Time Fire Radiative Power) is the result of a comprehensive improvement in quality and accuracy of hotspot detection, and user-friendliness of the product format, thanks to positive feedback by fire experts and users.

EUMETView contains visualisations for both Sentinel-3A and Sentinel-3B.

$schema ./collection_schema_v2-15.json hierarchyLevel series collectionType Dataset abstract The Copernicus NRT S3 FRP product identifies the location, and quantifies the radiative power (in MegaWatts), emitted by any hotspot present on land and ocean surfaces, that radiates a heating signal within a pixel size of 1 km2, in both daytime and nighttime conditions. All threatening hotspots are identified and characterised within 3h after SLSTR observation sensing time.

The latest Collection 3.2 of the NRT S3 FRP product (see Collection 3.2 of Sentinel-3 Near Real Time Fire Radiative Power) is the result of a comprehensive improvement in quality and accuracy of hotspot detection, and user-friendliness of the product format, thanks to positive feedback by fire experts and users. The FRP products for Africa are derived by geographically filtering for products over the African continent and islands as area of interest. abstractFormatted The Copernicus NRT S3 FRP product identifies the location, and quantifies the radiative power (in MegaWatts), emitted by any hotspot present on land and ocean surfaces, that radiates a heating signal within a pixel size of 1 km2, in both daytime and nighttime conditions. _source.abstract:
The products contain the typical altimetry measurements, like the altimeter range, the sea surface height, the wind speed, significant wave height and all required geophysical corrections and related flags. Also the sea Ice freeboard measurement is included.

The measurements in the standard data file provide the measurements in low (1 Hz = approx. 7km) and high resolution (20 Hz = approx. 300 m), in LRM mode or in SAR mode, for both C-band and Ku band. The SAR mode is the default mode. The reduced measurement data file contains 1 Hz measurements only. The enhanced measurement data file contains also the waveforms and associated parameters and the pseudo LRM measurements when in SAR mode.

Sentinel-3 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme. This collection contains reprocessed data from baseline collection 004. Operational data can be found in the corresponding collection.

_source.abstract:
This product is an RGB composite based upon data from Sentinel-3 OLCI level 1b NRT top of atmosphere (TOA) radiances from bands 0a08_radiance (Red), Oa06_radiance (Green) and Oa03_radiance (Blue), corrected for Rayleigh scattering and solar path length.

The primary objective of Sentinel-3 OLCI is to measure the colour of the ocean and land surface and provide information on ocean and land characteristics related to this (e.g. biology). OLCI also provides information on atmospheric composition and contributes to climate studies. This layer accentuates ocean colour; the change in the colour of the ocean, and other water bodies such as lakes, due to the substances dissolved and particles suspended within the water.

The images are generated with a pixel resolution of 0.06 degrees. Each step in the layer shows an individual orbit for Sentinel-3A. This layer can be exported from EUMETView as an via the Web Map Service (WMS).

Sentinel-3 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme.

_source.abstract:
SRAL level 1b: Complex echoes (In-phase (I) and Quadrature (Q)) for the Low Resolution Mode (LRM) and/or Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) mode both for C Band and Ku band. When the altimeter is in SAR mode, this product also contains the so-called Pseudo LRM (PLRM) echoes. Sentinel-3 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme.

_source.abstract:
Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) defines the fraction of Photosynthetically Active Radiation (400-700 nm) absorbed by the green parts of the canopy, and thus expresses the canopy's energy absorption capacity. FAPAR depends on canopy structure, leaf and soil optical properties and irradiance conditions. FAPAR has been recognized as one of the fundamental terrestrial state variables in the context of the global change sciences. It is a key variable in models assessing vegetation primary productivity and, more generally, in carbon cycle models implementing up-to-date land surfaces process schemes. Besides, FAPAR it is an indicator of the health of vegetation. FAPAR is generally well correlated with the Leaf Area Index, the more for healthy fully developed vegetation canopies.
This data record ETFAPAR-R (LSA-457) is available from January 2007 to June 2021 and is complemented and consistent with the near-real time product ETFAPAR (LSA-409).

_source.abstract:
This is a reprocessed dataset at baseline F06, which is continued by the NRT/NTC data stream from 29/April/2022 onwards. The level 2 high resolution products contain the typical altimetry measurements, like the altimeter range, the sea surface height, the wind speed, significant wave height and all required geophysical corrections and related flags derived either from RAW or RMC, or the combination of both.

Two measurement data files are available (standard and reduced), each with a different number of variables:
- The standard data file includes 1 Hz and 20 Hz measurements for the Ku- band as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz and some at 20 Hz.
- The reduced data file contains only 1 Hz measurements for the Ku- and C-bands as well as geophysical corrections at 1 Hz.

Note that the HR data products only contain Ku-band measurements. These products are suitable for users seeking information on sea state and those creating downstream added value products from multiple altimeters. Particularly for those seeking the highest resolution measurements.

Sentinel-6 is part of a series of Sentinel satellites, under the umbrella of the EU Copernicus programme. It is a collaborative Copernicus mission, implemented and co-funded by the European Commission, ESA, EUMETSAT and the USA, through NASA and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

_source.abstract:
Derived LST (DLST; LSA-003) provides a synthesis of the Meteosat Land Surface Temperature (MLST; LSA-001) products within a 10-day interval, consisting of two sub-products. LSA-003B contains a set of so-called Thermal Surface Parameters (TSP), obtained by fitting a diurnal temperature cycle model to the MLST composites provided by the companion sub-product LSA-003A.

The TSP summarise the thermal behaviour of the land surface for the 10-day interval and require about 10 times less storage space than the composites. TSP have physical meaning and direct relevance to land surface applications, including minimum temperature (around sunrise), temperature amplitude, and time of maximum temperature.

_source.abstract:
Reprocessed level 1b data from the Advanced Scatterometer (ASCAT) on Metop-A, resampled at 25 km Swath Grid (SZO). Normalized radar cross section (NRCS) triplets of the Earth surface together with:

- measurement time
- location (latitude and longitude)
- geometrical information (incidence and azimuth angles)

The prime objective of the Advanced SCATterometer (ASCAT) is to measure wind speed and direction over the oceans, and the main operational application is the assimilation of ocean winds in NWP models. Other operational applications, based on the use of measurements of the backscattering coefficient, are:

- sea ice edge detection and monitoring
- monitoring sea ice, snow cover, soil moisture and surface parameters

This product is also available at full resolution and at 12.5 km Swath Grid. This is a Fundamental Climate Data Record (FCDR).

_source.abstract:
The JAXA Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 3 (AMSR3), launched on June 29, 2025 aboard the GOSAT-GW satellite, measures multi-frequency microwave emissions across 12 frequencies and 21 channels (6.9 to 183 GHz).

EUMETSAT receives from JAXA GOSAT-GW AMSR3 level 1b and level 1r (resampled resolution) data in netCDF and converts the data into BUFR. Both netCDF and BUFR format data are provided.

- AMSR3 L1b Brightness Temperature: Calibrated microwave brightness temperatures derived from AMSR3 level 1a antenna-temperature measurements using radiometric conversion coefficients. The product contains multi-frequency, multi-polarization brightness temperature observations of microwave emission from the Earth's surface and atmosphere, together with associated observation geometry and geolocation information.
- AMSR3 L1r Resampled Brightness Temperature: Microwave brightness temperatures spatially resampled from the L1b product to align the field-of-view (FOV) center positions of the different AMSR3 frequency bands. Resampling is performed using weighting coefficients, with geolocation adjusted to the 89 GHz A-channel reference positions.

The product contains multi-frequency, multi-polarization brightness temperature observations of microwave emission from the Earth's surface and atmosphere, together with associated observation geometry and geolocation information.
- **AMSR3 L1r Resampled Brightness Temperature**: Microwave brightness temperatures spatially resampled from the L1b product to align the field-of-view (FOV) center positions of the different AMSR3 frequency bands. Resampling is performed using weighting coefficients, with geolocation adjusted to the 89 GHz A-channel reference positions.

_source.abstract:
The CACATOES database is a level 3 product derived from the TOOCAN database derived from Meteosat First and Second Generation MVIRI and SEVIRI measurements. Due to the large volume of TOOCAN data, a data reduction step is first performed by projecting the raw cloud systems data onto a regular 1°x1° grid, where all information about the systems is retained (see the Methods section of Roca and Fiolleau 2020 for more details). Statistics are then built from this reduced dataset, also known as CACATOES.

CACATOES allows to analyse the Deep Convective Cloud Systems (DCS) over the tropical belt by an Eulerian approach. The integrated morphological parameters of each DCS have been projected into a 1°x1°/1day grid. The characteristics of all the DCSs occurring in a given grid box have been sorted according to the DCS area occupied within this grid box. Thus, the most representative cloud system can then be easily identified for a given 1°x1°/1day grid box.

The data are available for region with boundaries 40° S to 40° N and 55° W to 55° E for the 1981-2023 period. The data has been used to reveal changes in convective organisation over tropical Africa and Atlantic Ocean (Rocal et al., 2024). The CATATOES data are available as 1°x1°/1day monthly files in netCDF.

_source.abstract:
Low Resolution Sea Ice Drift product covers both Northern Hemisphere (NH) and Southern Hemisphere (SH), all year round. Ice motion vectors with a time span of 48 hours are estimated by an advanced cross-correlation method (the Continuous MCC, CMCC) from pairs of passive and active microwave satellite images. Several single-sensor products are available, as well as a merged (multi-sensor) product. Maps of uncertainties are embedded in the product files.

Due to higher atmospheric wetness and sea ice surface melting, it is more challenging to track ice motion during summer. Accordingly:
- NH product files distributed between 1 May and 30 September have larger uncertainties and more interpolated vectors.
- SH product files between 1 November and 30 March have the same limitation.

_source.abstract:
As part of its commercial radio occultation (RO) service, the ROM SAF generates profile products derived from measurements by RO instruments based on the following satellite and procured data sets:

- Spire RO data procured by EUMETSAT from the contractor Spire, originating from the STRATOS RO payload;
- RO data procured by NOAA from various contractors, depending on delivery order.

The RO technique utilises the bending due to refraction of GNSS radio signals as they pass through the Earth's atmosphere. Each occultation event gives a bending angle and a vertical profile of atmospheric refractivity, from which temperature, pressure, and humidity profiles are retrieved. The RO profile data have a global coverage and are insensitive to clouds and the underlying surface.

 The ROM SAF commercial RO NRT level 2 profile products are provided in the netCDF and BUFR formats and include the following geophysical variables:

- Refractivity profiles based on Spire (operational product)
- Refractivity profiles based on commercial RO data from NOAA (best effort product)

 In addition, the following auxiliary geophysical variables are generated and included in the netCDF and BUFR files:

- Bending angle (copy of level 1b data generated by EUMETSAT Secretariat)
- Dry temperature profiles
- Temperature profiles
- Specific humidity profiles
- Pressure profiles
- Surface pressure

_source.abstract:
The Sea Ice Index is a climate indicator of sea-ice coverage. The index covers both the sea-ice extent and area over the last 40+ years and is continuously updated to present time. It consists of:
- An updated series of graphs (.png) visualising the trends and evolution of sea ice at hemispheric, global and regional scales.
- Data files (.txt and .nc) for users who are interested in analysing and plotting the data themselves.

The Sea Ice Index is derived from the OSI SAF Global Sea Ice Concentration data, with R&D input from ESA CCI.

_source.abstract:
Evapotranspiration (ET) represents the flux of water transferred from the Earth–atmosphere interface through evaporation (from soil, water bodies, and canopy interception) and transpiration by vegetation. ET is a key component of the water cycle and is associated with the latent heat flux (LE), which links the energy and water cycles. It is complemented by the sensible heat flux (MH), representing the turbulent heat exchanges at the Earth–atmosphere interface. Together, surface energy and water fluxes play a crucial role in weather forecasting, global climate monitoring, water resource management, agriculture, and ecological studies.
This data record provides 30 minute ET (LSA 350 MET R), MLE (LSA 353 MLE R), and MH (LSA 352 MH R), as well as daily ET (LSA 351 DMET R), which is obtained by integrating the 30 minute ET estimates. _source.abstract:
The level 2 (L2) Copernicus Sentinel-3 Near Real Time (NRT) Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) product quantifies the abundance of aerosol particles, and monitors their global distribution and long-range transport, at the scale of 9.5 x 9.5 km2. All observations are made available in less than 3 hours from the SLSTR observation sensing time. It is only applicable during daytime.

The product is generated from the reference 'optimised Simultaneous Surface Aerosol Retrieval for Copernicus Sentinel-3' (OSSAR-CS3) processor, dedicated to processing SLSTR data, and procured by EUMETSAT on behalf of the European Commission.

The following Baseline Collections (BC) have been released so far:

- Collection 1.0: released on 27/08/2020, effective until 28/10/2021, with quality status pre-operational for the AOD Ocean product and demonstrational for the AOD Land product.
- Collection 2.0: released on 28/10/2021, effective until 03/11/2022, upgrading the quality status of the AOD Land product from demonstrational to pre-operational.
- Collection 3.0: released on 03/11/2022, with no change to the quality status.

Note: Partial reprocessing is being done by EUMETSAT based on user requests. Please contact the EUMETSAT User Helpdesk if you wish to access previous data with the latest collection. All Sentinel-3 Near Real Time (NRT) products are available at pick-up point in less than 3h.

_source.abstract:
Stress-equivalent 10m winds over the global oceans obtained from the ScatSat-1 OSCAT scatterometer are derived from the satellite's Ku-band radar measurements of ocean surface roughness. The ScatSat-1 mission, launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), carries an Oceansat-2 Scatterometer (OSCAT) that measures normalized radar cross-section (sigma-0) values from the ocean surface. These sigma-0 measurements are then converted to stress-equivalent winds using specialized geophysical model functions that account for the relationship between wind stress and surface roughness.

The stress-equivalent wind approach differs from traditional neutral stability winds by directly relating to the momentum flux (wind stress) at the ocean surface, making these winds particularly valuable for:

- Ocean circulation modeling
- Air-sea interaction studies
- Wind stress curl calculations
- Climate research

The ScatSat-1 OSCAT operates at 13.515 GHz with dual polarization (HH and VV) and provides measurements across a 1800 km wide swath with spatial resolution of approximately 50 km. The instrument uses a rotating dish antenna with two feeds that generate a conical scanning pattern, allowing it to observe each point on the ocean surface from multiple azimuth angles. This multi-angle viewing geometry is crucial for resolving the wind direction ambiguity inherent in scatterometer measurements.

The wind retrieval process involves several steps:

- Collection of sigma-0 measurements at multiple azimuth angles
- Application of quality control filters to remove rain contamination and land effects
- Inversion of the geophysical model function to obtain wind vector solutions
- Selection of the most probable wind direction from multiple ambiguous solutions using external information or median filtering

The stress-equivalent winds are calibrated and validated against buoy measurements and other satellite wind products to ensure accuracy and consistency with the global observing system.
_source.abstractFormatted:
Stress-equivalent 10m winds over the global oceans obtained from the ScatSat-1 OSCAT scatterometer are derived from the satellite's Ku-band radar measurements of ocean surface roughness. The ScatSat-1 mission, launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), carries an Oceansat-2 Scatterometer (OSCAT) that measures normalized radar cross-section (sigma-0) values from the ocean surface. These sigma-0 measurements are then converted to stress-equivalent winds using specialized geophysical model functions that account for the relationship between wind stress and surface roughness.

The stress-equivalent wind approach differs from traditional neutral stability winds by directly relating to the momentum flux (wind stress) at the ocean surface, making these winds particularly valuable for:

- Ocean circulation modeling
- Air-sea interaction studies
- Wind stress curl calculations
- Climate research

The ScatSat-1 OSCAT operates at 13.515 GHz with dual polarization (HH and VV) and provides measurements across a 1800 km wide swath with spatial resolution of approximately 50 km. The instrument uses a rotating dish antenna with two feeds that generate a conical scanning pattern, allowing it to observe each point on the ocean surface from multiple azimuth angles. This multi-angle viewing geometry is crucial for resolving the wind direction ambiguity inherent in scatterometer measurements.

The wind retrieval process involves several steps:

- Collection of sigma-0 measurements at multiple azimuth angles
- Application of quality control filters to remove rain contamination and land effects
- Inversion of the geophysical model function to obtain wind vector solutions
- Selection of the most probable wind direction from multiple ambiguous solutions using external information or median filtering

The stress-equivalent winds are calibrated and validated against buoy measurements and other satellite wind products to ensure accuracy and consistency with the global observing system.

_source.abstract:
Fraction of Vegetation cover (FVC) defines an important structural property of a plant canopy, which corresponds to the complement to unity of the gap fraction at nadir direction, accounting for the amount of vegetation distributed in a horizontal perspective. FVC is related with the partition between soil and vegetation contribution for emissivity and temperature. This property is necessary for describing land surface processes and surface parameterisation schemes used for climate and weather forecasting. Besides, the FVC is relevant for a wide range of Land Biosphere Applications such as agriculture and forestry, environmental management and land use, hydrology, natural hazards monitoring and management, vegetation-soil dynamics monitoring, drought conditions and fire scar extent.
This data record ETFVC-R (LSA-455) is available from January 2007 to June 2021 and is complemented and consistent with the near-real time product ETFVC (LSA-403).

_source.abstract:
The MWS level 1b radiance product consists of time-referenced, geolocated and calibrated top of the atmosphere spectral radiance measurements.  The radiances are quality controlled, spectrally characterised, and annotated with satellite position and pointing information. The product also contains the brightness temperatures corresponding to the radiances of all MWS channels. For each scanline, the L1b data is available for all ninety five earth view pixels. The regional MWS L1b product is available at a higher temporal frequency  compared to the global product, with the coverage limited to Europe,  North Atlantic region, and parts of Africa and the Indian Ocean.

The MWS instrument is a passive, across-track scanning radiometer capable of measuring thermal radiance emitted by the Earth and the atmosphere over twenty four spectral bands in a frequency range from 23.8 GHz to 229 GHz.

The primary role of MWS is to provide temperature and humidity atmosphere sounding information. The main application of MWS L1b data is in Numerical Weather Prediction where the data is directly assimilated in NWP models.  The MWS data also extends the long term climate records from microwave sounding sensors.

The data is available in BUFR format under collection reference EO:EUM:DAT:0892.

_source.abstract:
A subset of the Metop-SG products is provided in BUFR format. The following global and regional products from Metop-SGA satellite are available in BUFR format.

- Global GRAS-2 L1b (available from 26 February 2026)
- Global MWS L1b (available from 11 June 2026)
- Global IASI-NG L1c (available from 7 October 2026)
- Regional MWS L1b (available from 12 November 2026)
- Regional RO L1b
- Regional IASI-NG L1c
- Global and Regional IASI-NG L1d
- Global and Regional IASI-NG L2
- Global METimage L2 AMV

At present, the global GRAS‑2 L1b, global and regional MWS L1b and global IASI-NG L1c products are the only Metop‑SG BUFR products released to users. The remaining Metop-SG products in BUFR format will be released once their respective calibration/validation activities are completed.

_source.abstract:
The OPERA-SEVIRI-NORDLIS ML/AI Fusion Dataset is a static training dataset for machine learning and AI applications. It combines ground-based weather radar, lightning and geostationary satellite observations over Europe on one common grid, and covers the years 2018 to 2023. It contains the EUMETNET OPERA radar composites of maximum reflectivity, rainfall rate and 1-hour rainfall accumulation at 15-minute intervals, each with a quality indicator. It also contains MSG SEVIRI Rapid Scan Service level 1.5 data in all 12 channels at 5-minute intervals, provided as reflectances and brightness temperatures together with sun and satellite angles. Finally, it includes NORDLIS ground-based lightning observations over northern Europe, supplied by FMI Open Data under CC BY 4.0, as exact strike locations and times and as strike counts aggregated to the common grid.

All gridded data are on the OPERA composite grid: a Lambert Azimuthal Equal Area projection with 2 km × 2 km pixels (1900 × 2200). The SEVIRI data were reprojected from the geostationary projection with nearest-neighbour interpolation, so the original values and extremes are preserved. The data are provided as CF-compliant NetCDF files per time step, as a combined Zarr store and as Parquet files for the lightning strikes. They are intended for applications such as satellite-based precipitation estimation, filling gaps in radar coverage and nowcasting.

Conversion code repository: https://gitlab.eumetsat.int/data-curation/opera-seviri-data-cube
